blocks.text: 1. Causal Masking
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446020362-412031845.png

Feed-Forward Networks, the previous topic, covered the second sublayer within every Transformer layer. Causal Masking is a mechanism ensuring the decoder cannot look ahead at future positions, explored throughout this topic.
It delivers the exact safeguard already previewed in The Decoder, a genuinely essential, mathematically precise mechanism covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to a preview of why order genuinely matters here, already covered in The Decoder. The decoder's own Self-Attention genuinely must not look ahead at future, not-yet-generated positions, already covered there.
This topic genuinely delivers the direct, mathematical mechanism already previewed there, closing the exact gap already identified at that earlier point in this course.
3. Why Looking Ahead Is Genuinely A Problem

blocks.alt: Why Looking Ahead Is Genuinely A Problem
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021405-82368261.png
This connects back to sequential word generation, already covered in Image Captioning. At inference time, already covered there, future words genuinely do not exist yet to be attended to.

Training must genuinely match that exact same real-world constraint, otherwise the decoder would genuinely learn to rely on information it will never actually have available when genuinely generating new text.
4. The Core Idea

Causal Masking's genuinely core idea connects back to Self-Attention within the decoder, already covered in The Decoder. Genuinely block each position from attending to any position that comes after it.
This genuinely direct, simple rule, already covered in this section, is the entire fix this topic introduces, directly enforcing the constraint already covered as necessary in the previous section.

blocks.text: 5. The Masking Mechanism
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021406-633744224.png
This connects back to Softmax, already covered in the Activation Functions module. Set the genuinely relevance scores for forbidden, future positions to genuinely negative infinity before Softmax.
Softmax genuinely then assigns those positions an attention weight of essentially exactly zero, a genuinely elegant, direct way of implementing the core idea already covered in the previous section.
6. Why Negative Infinity Specifically
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021407-271768445.png
This connects back to Softmax's own exponential function, already covered in the Activation Functions module. The exponential of negative infinity genuinely equals exactly zero.

This guarantees those forbidden positions genuinely contribute nothing at all to the final weighted sum, a genuinely precise, mathematically guaranteed way of enforcing the masking already covered in the previous section.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: In practice, already covered in this topic, implementations typically use a genuinely very large negative number rather than literal infinity, since actual infinite values can cause numerical issues on real hardware.

blocks.text: 7. Visualizing The Triangular Mask
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021408-546348980.png

A genuinely helpful, common visualization connects back to the attention weights matrix, already covered throughout the Attention Mechanism module. The allowed positions genuinely form a lower triangular pattern within that matrix.

This genuinely visual pattern, already covered in this section, makes the core idea already covered earlier in this topic genuinely easy to picture: each row can only genuinely look at columns up to and including itself.
8. The Encoder Does Not Need This

blocks.alt: The Encoder Does Not Need This
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021408-971233036.png

This connects back to Self-Attention within the encoder, already covered in The Encoder. The encoder genuinely has no such restriction, since the entire input is genuinely already fully available at once.

This is a genuinely important, real contrast between how the encoder and decoder each use Self-Attention, directly explaining why Causal Masking, already covered throughout this topic, applies specifically and only to the decoder.

blocks.text: 9. A Genuine Training-Time Efficiency Benefit

A genuinely important, real practical benefit connects back to the parallelization benefit, already covered in Self-Attention. Causal Masking genuinely lets the entire target sequence be processed in parallel during training.
This is a genuinely valuable, real practical benefit, since the mask alone genuinely enforces the correct constraint without requiring genuinely slow, sequential processing during training itself.
10. Recognizing Why Causal Masking Is Genuinely Essential

blocks.alt: Recognizing Why Causal Masking Is Genuinely Essential
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021409-328437704.png

This connects back to any decoder generating output sequentially, already covered throughout this course. Causal Masking, already covered in this topic, directly enforces the genuinely honest, realistic training constraint needed.

This connects forward to Large Language Models, covered later in this course, built around genuinely this exact masking pattern. Understanding it now, already covered, is genuinely essential preparation.
11. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates constructing and applying a causal mask to a genuinely small attention score matrix, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

sequence_length = 5
raw_scores = np.random.RandomState(42).normal(size=(sequence_length, sequence_length))

# already covered as visualizing the triangular mask in this topic
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((sequence_length, sequence_length)), k=1).astype(bool)

masked_scores = raw_scores.copy()
masked_scores[causal_mask] = -np.inf  # already covered as the masking mechanism in this topic

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

attention_weights = softmax(masked_scores)  # already covered as why negative infinity specifically in this topic

print("Attention weights (each row can only genuinely attend to itself and earlier positions):")
print(np.round(attention_weights, 3))
print("\nNotice every row's own upper-right values are genuinely exactly zero, already covered as the triangular mask in this topic")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the resulting attention weights forming a genuinely clean lower triangular pattern, with every forbidden future position getting a weight of genuinely exactly zero, exactly the mechanism already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Causal Masking ensures the decoder cannot look ahead at future, not-yet-generated positions.
At inference time, future words genuinely do not exist yet, so training must match that constraint.
It blocks each position from attending to any position that comes after it.
Relevance scores for forbidden positions get set to negative infinity before Softmax.
The exponential of negative infinity equals zero, guaranteeing no contribution from those positions.
The allowed positions form a lower triangular pattern within the attention matrix.
The encoder does not need this, since the entire input is already fully available at once.
It lets the entire target sequence be processed in parallel during training, despite the constraint.
